input.content: Pattern: "simplification" that drops an ownership guard before a destructive dict/state removal. In cleanup_setup(store, workspace_id, setup_id), the guard `association and association["setup_id"] == setup_id` was removed, leaving an unconditional `store.active.pop(workspace_id, None)`. This makes a queued cleanup for a FAILED/old setup delete the active association owned by a DIFFERENT, later setup that completed in the interim — silently losing a valid connection (active_connection returns None). Lesson: a conditional guard keyed on an identity/ownership field (setup_id/version/owner) before pop/delete is usually load-bearing for last-writer/interleaving correctness; "redundant if" simplifications must be checked against documented interleavings. Existing happy-path test (cleanup of own association) stays green and does not cover the cross-setup interleaving — green implementation-shaped tests do not prove the ownership contract.
